title: 2013 AMC 12A Problem 17
statement: A group of \(12\) pirates agree to divide a treasure chest of gold coins among themselves as follows. The \(k\)th pirate to take a share takes \(\dfrac{k}{12}\) of the coins that remain in the chest. The number of coins initially in the chest is the smallest number for which this arrangement will allow each pirate to receive a positive whole number of coins. How many coins does the \(12\)th pirate receive?

solutions.text:
For \(1 \le k \le 11,\) the number of coins before the \(k\)th pirate takes a share is \(\dfrac{12}{12 - k}\) times the number afterward. So if \(n\) coins are left for the \(12\)th pirate, the initial count is \[ \dfrac{12^{11}\, n}{11!} = \dfrac{2^{14}\cdot 3^{7}\, n}{5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11}. \]

The smallest \(n\) making this a positive integer is \(5^2\cdot7\cdot11=1925.\) Before pirate \(k,\) the remaining count is the initial count multiplied by \(\frac{11!}{(12-k)!\,12^{k-1}};\) substituting this \(n\) shows it is an integer for every \(k.\) Hence all shares are integral, and the \(12\)th pirate receives \(1925\) coins.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Before the \(k\)th pirate takes a share, the chest holds \(\dfrac{12}{12 - k}\) times what remains after
